title: Regular quotient ideal intersection inclusion
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I an ideal, and gs a list whose images in R/I form a regular sequence. Then I ∩ Ideal.ofList gs ≤ I * Ideal.ofList gs.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0665, proof lines 7487-7494

proof.text: Restrict the regularity hypothesis from the quotient ring to R using Mathlib RingTheory.Sequence.isWeaklyRegular_map_algebraMap_iff. Apply RingTheory.Sequence.map_first_exact_on_four_term_right_exact_of_isSMulRegular_last to the exact sequence 0 → I → R → R/I → 0. Exactness of 0 → I is LinearMap.exact_zero_iff_injective and subtype_injective; exactness at R is LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ, and the quotient map is surjective.

For x ∈ I ∩ Ideal.ofList gs, let xi be x viewed as an element of I. Since x belongs to Ideal.ofList gs, its class in R / ((Ideal.ofList gs) • R) is zero. Exactness of the induced maps gives that the class of xi in I / ((Ideal.ofList gs) • I) is in the image of the zero map, hence is zero. Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero gives xi ∈ (Ideal.ofList gs) • I; Submodule.mem_smul_top_iff identifies this with x ∈ (Ideal.ofList gs) • I inside R. Ideal.smul_eq_mul and commutativity give x ∈ I * Ideal.ofList gs.
